# Independent review — LV cable sizing, Building 4210 (P-4210)

Scope reviewed: `/filesystem/electrical__lv_cable_sizing__blind/output/submission.zip` (5 files), against task.md, EDS-26 Rev 4, G-001, UFC 3-501-01, UFC 3-520-01, M-501-C, GEO-4210-T, E-619/E-618/E-611/E-612/E-613/E-615/E-616, the schedules, Cascadia data/price list and the unit price book. I re-derived lengths, ampacities, voltage drops, duct temperatures, EGCs and the ledger from the source documents; I did not reuse the author's scripts. Findings are most serious first.

---

## 1. BLOCKING — F-05 has three parallel sets but only one duct is assigned; the duct assignment is incomplete and, as documented, violates the one-set-per-duct and 40 % fill rules

**Requirement.** Task.md §1 (`duct_ids` "names the duct each set occupies, for duct-bank circuits only"); task.md §3 `duct_assignment` "one row per parallel set of each duct-bank circuit"; EDS-26 Rev 4 6.2 "One three-phase set occupies one duct; a duct must not carry conductors of more than one circuit"; EDS-26 6.1 40 % fill; Section 26 05 33 3.2 "One three-phase circuit per duct." The task's 25 hard families explicitly include "the duct assignment in the design basis".

**What the deliverable has.**
- `wire_schedule.csv`, circuit F-05: `sets = 3`, `size = 600 kcmil`, `material = AL`, `duct_ids = E1` (one duct named for three sets). The E-621 DXF abbreviation note itself says "DUCTS = ... ONE DUCT PER SET", yet the F-05 row has one ID for three sets.
- `calc_book.xlsx`, sheet `duct_assignment`: only 9 rows — SE-1 sets 1-6, F-10 sets 1-2, and **F-05 set 1 only** (`E1`). Sets 2 and 3 of F-05 have no row.
- `design_basis.md`, JSON `duct_assignment`: `"F-05": ["E1"]`; prose §6: "F-05: one set in E1 (alone in DB-2, so no mutual heating)." The same one-set statement is in the author's summary. The design basis contradicts itself: §4 correctly says "F-05 runs **three parallel sets** of 600 kcmil aluminium", while §6 assigns one set to one duct.
- The cost ledger and voltage-drop calculation, by contrast, use **three** F-05 sets (600 kcmil AL: 6,444 ft = 3 sets × 3 phases × 716 ft; six 600 kcmil terminations; 2,148 ft of 3/0 EGC = 3 × 716).

**What it should be.** F-05 needs three ducts, one per set. DB-2 has three available ducts (E1, E2, E3; E4 is reserved for communications, E-619). `duct_ids` should read `E1,E2,E3`; `duct_assignment` should have rows F-05 set 1 → E1, set 2 → E2, set 3 → E3; the design-basis JSON/prose and the mutual-heating value for F-05 must reflect three loaded ducts (not "alone"/0 K).

**Evidence / consequence.** If the only named duct E1 is used for all three sets, 9 × 600 kcmil AL conductors (OD 0.948 in, area 0.7058 in² each) occupy 6.352 in² of a 4-in EPC-40 duct (internal area 12.730 in²) = **49.9 % fill, above the 40 % limit of EDS-26 6.1**, and three sets share one duct contrary to EDS-26 6.2. Under the task's scoring rule, "a cheap package that fails any of its hard families keeps none of [O′]"; this hard-family failure therefore withholds the package's entire installed-cost credit, not just F-05's. If the other two sets are placed elsewhere, the deliverable does not say where — a constructability and register failure. My EDS-26 5.3 calculation with the three F-05 sets in E1/E2/E3 gives dT ≈ 1.50 K and 399.9 A per set; the 75 °C termination cap of 336 A still governs, so the 336 A selection itself remains valid — but the hard-family duct assignment is not satisfied. Register R0121 ("one duct per set; ten ducts used in DB-1 and one in DB-2, no duct shared") and R0122 ("Applied in the duct assignment") are therefore false: DB-1 uses **8** loaded ducts (SE-1 6 + F-10 2), and DB-2 should use **3**, not one.


---

## 2. MAJOR — B-08 is declared at 45 °C; M-501-C requires 40 °C for that circuit

**Requirement.** M-501-C ambient table: ceiling cavity/return plenum = 40 °C; the 45 °C row applies to "every circuit whose whole run is inside [mechanical room 121 and fire pump room 105], and the feeders entering them: MCC-1, the fire pump, and the motor branch circuits fed from MCC-1." M-501-C note 3: every circuit routed on E-611/E-612/E-616 other than those named in the 45 °C row takes the ceiling-cavity 40 °C. EDS-26 5.2 requires the ambient of the space the raceway passes through from M-501-C.

**What the deliverable has.** `wire_schedule.csv`, B-08: `ambient_c = 45.0`; DXF B-08 `AMB C` 45.0. B-08 is fed from **LP-1** to KEF-1 and is routed on E-611; it is not MCC-1, the fire pump, or a motor branch fed from MCC-1. The author's own register agrees: R0133 (40 °C) lists B-08 and R0128 (45 °C) does not.

**What it should be.** 40 °C. The 90 °C ampacity at 40 °C is 54 × 0.9129 = 49.3 A; the governing 60 °C termination cap is 40 A either way, so the 8 AWG selection is still adequate, but the declared ambient and the hard ambient family for B-08 are wrong and conflict with the register.

**Evidence.** M-501-C p.1 rows and note 3; connected load schedule B-08 (from LP-1, routed E-611); `constraint_register.xlsx` R0128/R0133; `wire_schedule.csv` row B-08. This is the only circuit whose schedule ambient contradicts the memo. The conductor is safe either way, but if the verifier checks the declared `ambient_c` against M-501-C, B-08's hard ambient family fails and the package O′ is withheld under the same rule.


---

## 3. MAJOR (register precision / false hard-row) — R0012 applies the "not less than the branch device rating" rule to B-17, a motor feeder whose 6 AWG ampacity (54 A) is below its 60 A OCPD

**Requirement.** EDS-26 2.1: "Branch-circuit conductors supplying **lighting, receptacle and hard-wired appliance loads** are sized for not less than the rating of the branch device." EDS-26 2.1.1: for a motor, an A/C unit, an ASD, an elevator, a fire pump or a transformer "the conductor is sized on the load alone ... and the device rating is **NOT** a floor." NFPA 70 430.22/430.52 permit a motor branch OCPD above the conductor ampacity.

**What the deliverable has.** `constraint_register.xlsx` R0012 is HARD, text as above, with `applies_to = "B-01 to B-10, B-16 to B-18"` and resolution "Design current = branch device rating: 20, 40, 60, 100 A". B-17 is a motor feeder (shop air compressor CMP-1, 15 hp, motor schedule; connected-load class "Motor feeder"), OCPD 60 A, 125 % FLA design current 43.25 A, 6 AWG with 60 °C ampacity 54 A. B-08 is also a motor feeder (KEF-1, 5 hp), 30 A OCPD, design 17.75 A, 8 AWG 40 A.

**What it should be.** R0012 should apply only to the lighting, receptacle and hard-wired appliance circuits (B-01 to B-07, B-09, B-10, B-16, B-18), not to B-08 or B-17; those are governed by R0013/EDS-26 2.1.1, and B-17's 54 A < 60 A is expressly permitted for a motor branch (430.22/430.52; the overload, not the branch OCPD, protects the conductor). As written, the register contains a HARD row that lists B-17 and is numerically unsatisfied, which is exactly the "registered but not satisfied" condition the task penalises. The schedule itself is compliant: B-17 `design_current_a = 43.25`, `corrected_ampacity_a = 54`, `ocpd_a = 60`, and its `governing_constraint` correctly says ampacity/termination (not the device floor). The register resolution's "20, 40, 60, 100 A" also omits B-08's 30 A and misstates B-08/B-17 design currents.

**Evidence.** register R0012 and R0013; EDS-26 2.1 and 2.1.1; connected load schedule B-17 (OCPD 60, load 34.6); motor schedule CMP-1 (15 hp, 34.6 FLA); `wire_schedule.csv` B-17 (6 CU, amp 54, OCPD 60, design 43.25). If the verifier applies R0012 as written to B-17, this HARD row is registered but not satisfied (54 A < 60 A), so B-17's h would fail and the package O′ would be withheld; the correct fix is to remove B-08/B-17 from R0012's `applies_to`.


---

## 4. MAJOR — The service-entrance "not reducible" conclusion is wrong: five 600 kcmil Cu sets are feasible and about $1,262 cheaper

**Requirement.** Task.md §1: "minimise the installed cost of the conductor package"; EDS-26 8: "where two compliant selections exist, the lower installed cost governs." EDS-26 2.2/UFC 3-501-01 3-2.3.3 require SE-1 ampacity ≥ 2000 A (MSB-1 bus).

**What the deliverable has.** SE-1 = 6 sets × 500 kcmil Cu, 6 × 371.5 = 2,229 A. Design basis §5: "This is the largest single cost of the package and it is not reducible: five sets of 600 kcmil carry only 2064 A and cost more, and six sets of 400 kcmil reach only 1993 A once mutual heating is included."

**What it should be.** Five 600 kcmil Cu sets in the best available DB-1 positions (D1, D2, D3, D9, D10, with F-10 in D4, D8) give, by the EDS-26 5.3 Neher-McGrath calculation with the same loads (SE-1 1732/5 = 346.4 A per set; F-10 432/2 = 216 A per duct), a minimum set ampacity of **403.7 A** → **2,018.5 A ≥ 2,000 A** (the D2 set is the limiting one; the other sets are 406.0–420.3 A). 600 kcmil Cu is already one of the five standard sizes (F-05 uses 600 kcmil Al), 5 ≤ 6 terminals, and 600 ≤ 600 kcmil terminal max at T-1/MSB-1. Fill in a 5-in duct is 10.6 % and jam ratio 5.32, both compliant.

**Cost evidence (Cascadia price list, 6 % quantity break):** 6 × 500 Cu: phase 5,760 ft × $6.25 = $36,000.00; 4/0 EGC 1,920 ft × $2.876 = $5,521.92; 500 kcmil terminations 12 × $193 = $2,316.00; gross $43,837.92. 5 × 600 Cu: phase 4,800 ft × $7.42 = $35,616.00; EGC 1,600 ft × $2.876 = $4,601.60; 600 kcmil terminations 10 × $228 = $2,280.00; gross $42,497.60. Net of the 6 % conductor break the saving is **≈ $1,262** (total length still 39,752 ft ≥ 38,000 ft). The design basis's "2064 A" is not reproducible from the EDS-26 5.3 calculation (the loaded best arrangement gives 2018.5 A) and the "cost more" claim is arithmetically false; the selected 6 × 500 is compliant but **not** cost-minimal. **Caveat:** the 5 × 600 option raises SE-1's own drop from 1.043 % to 1.1225 % (R 0.0240 vs 0.0278, 5 sets vs 6), so B-17's cumulative becomes 5.0075 % — above the nominal 5.0 % but inside the task's 0.02 percentage-point allowance; the author's 6 × 500 (4.928 %) has more margin. The alternative is therefore feasible within the stated tolerance, but tight on both ampacity (2018.5 A vs 2000 A) and voltage drop.

**Evidence.** My script implementing EDS-26 5.3 (all geometry from E-619; Rac(Tc) from Cascadia 4.1; dT_m at connected load/sets) reproduces the author's 371.5 A for 6 × 500 and gives 403.7 A min for 5 × 600 in D1/D2/D3/D9/D10. Price list rows 500/600 kcmil; ledger lines for SE-1.


---

## 5. MAJOR — Register row R0111 states F-05's EGC as 2/0, which would not satisfy NFPA 70 250.122(B); the schedule/ledger use 3/0

**Requirement.** EDS-26 5.7 / NFPA 70 250.122(B): where the phase conductor is increased above the ampacity-only size, increase the EGC in the same circular-mil ratio. ## 12. MINOR — Fire-pump locked-rotor narrative arithmetic is slightly off (3.09 % stated vs 3.07 % recomputed)

**Requirement.** EDS-26 4.6.3 / NFPA 70 695: 15 % at locked rotor, 5 % at rated current. The limit is met either way.

**What the deliverable has.** design_basis §4: "3.09 percent at 543 A locked rotor ... SE-1 contributes 1.42 percent and F-03 1.67 percent." Using the schedule's own SE-1 drop (1.043 % at 1600 A) and F-03 drop (0.295 % at 96 A): SE-1 at 1600 + 543 = 2,143 A gives 1.043 × 2143/1600 = **1.397 %**, F-03 at 543 A gives 0.295 × 543/96 = **1.670 %**, total **3.067 %**. The stated 1.42/3.09 is a small overstatement, not a compliance issue.


---

## 13. MINOR — Register R0068/R0121 resolutions misstate the DB-1 loading ("ten loaded/used" ducts)

**Requirement.** EDS-26 5.3.4 "Every duct carrying load contributes"; EDS-26 6.2 one set per duct.

**What the deliverable has.** R0068 resolution: "All ten loaded ducts of DB-1 included in every dT_m sum." R0121 resolution: "ten ducts used in DB-1 and one in DB-2, no duct shared." DB-1 has 10 **available** ducts, of which **8** are loaded/used (SE-1 D1,D2,D3,D5,D9,D10 and F-10 D4,D8); D6 and D7 are empty. DB-2 should have **3** used by F-05, not one. These statements are part of the same F-05/duct-assignment defect as finding 1.


---

## 14. MINOR — Register rows R0152 and R0154 each carry a list of several requirements, contrary to "one row states one requirement"

**Requirement.** Task.md §5: "One row states one requirement: a row is credited with at most one of them, and a row that cites several clauses at once, or carries a list of unrelated values, is not a register row and counts against precision."

**What the deliverable has.** R0152 (EDS-26 7.2) lists design temperatures, thermal properties, ampacity basis, load factor, termination allowance, VD start/limits, duct assignment, tray fill, sizes standardised and the cost ledger in one row. R0154 (EDS-26 7.4) lists codes of record, environmental parameters, VD budget, cost ledger and duct assignment in one row. These are multi-item rows; the author already has separate rows for many of the sub-items (R0059-R0079, R0143-R0149), but not all. R0154's resolution also says "sections 1 to 8", while the document-conflict table it relies on is section 9 of design_basis.md.

**What it should be.** Split into one row per requirement (or at least one row per deliverable element), keeping the values and applies_to specific. Evidence: register R0152/R0154; task.md §5.


---

## 15. MINOR — R0056 is an observation, not a requirement, and R0111/R0028 resolutions are inaccurate (already noted in findings 5 and 11)

**Requirement.** Task.md §5: one requirement per row; `value` is the number the requirement fixes.

**What the deliverable has.** R0056 (EDS-26 5.2) says "The neutral of a 120 V line-to-neutral circuit is a current-carrying conductor; there are no such circuits in this scope", value 0 count. The second clause is an observation about this project, not a requirement; the row is a candidate for precision loss. R0111's resolution (2/0 EGC) and R0028's resolution ("250 to 600 kcmil") are wrong as detailed in findings 5 and 11. Evidence: register R0056, R0111, R0028.

## 16. MINOR (declaration convention/risk) — `design_current_a` is the total circuit current on parallel circuits, while `corrected_ampacity_a` is per set; a direct comparison appears to fail on eight circuits

**Requirement.** Task.md §1: "`design_current_a` is the current the conductor's corrected ampacity had to carry; `corrected_ampacity_a` is the ampacity **per set**." `sets` is the number of parallel sets.

**What the deliverable has.** For every parallel circuit the CSV puts the **total** circuit current in `design_current_a` and the **per-set** ampacity in `corrected_ampacity_a`, relying on the reader to multiply by `sets`: F-01 600.0 vs 306.6 (2 sets); F-04 310.0 vs 171.9 (2); F-05 400.0 vs 336.0 (3); F-06 338.29 vs 195.0 (2); F-07 780.67 vs 263.0 (3); F-10 600.0 vs 330.7 (2); F-12 310.0 vs 171.9 (2); SE-1 2000.0 vs 371.5 (6). In each case `design_current_a > corrected_ampacity_a` even though `sets × corrected_ampacity_a` is adequate. The design basis §3 explains "the design current is compared with sets x ampacity per set", so the intent is recoverable, but the column text does not match the per-set definition literally.

**What it should be.** Either put the per-set design current (design total ÷ sets: 300, 155, 133.3, 169.1, 260.2, 300, 155, 333.3) in `design_current_a`, or make the total explicit and ensure the grader's check uses `sets`. As written, a verifier that compares `design_current_a ≤ corrected_ampacity_a` directly (the literal reading of the column pair) would mark eight circuits as ampacity failures. The underlying selections are all adequate (`sets × amp` ≥ design); this is a declaration/format risk, not a conductor selection error.

# Independent review — LV cable sizing, Building 4210 (P-4210)

Scope reviewed: `/filesystem/electrical__lv_cable_sizing__blind/output/submission.zip` (5 files), against task.md, EDS-26 Rev 4, G-001, UFC 3-501-01, UFC 3-520-01, M-501-C, GEO-4210-T, E-619/E-618/E-611/E-612/E-613/E-615/E-616, the schedules, Cascadia data/price list and the unit price book. I re-derived lengths, ampacities, voltage drops, duct temperatures, EGCs and the ledger from the source documents; I did not reuse the author's scripts. Findings are most serious first.

---

## 1. BLOCKING — F-05 has three parallel sets but only one duct is assigned; the duct assignment is incomplete and, as documented, violates the one-set-per-duct and 40 % fill rules

**Requirement.** Task.md §1 (`duct_ids` "names the duct each set occupies, for duct-bank circuits only"); task.md §3 `duct_assignment` "one row per parallel set of each duct-bank circuit"; EDS-26 Rev 4 6.2 "One three-phase set occupies one duct; a duct must not carry conductors of more than one circuit"; EDS-26 6.1 40 % fill; Section 26 05 33 3.2 "One three-phase circuit per duct." The task's 25 hard families explicitly include "the duct assignment in the design basis".

**What the deliverable has.**
- `wire_schedule.csv`, circuit F-05: `sets = 3`, `size = 600 kcmil`, `material = AL`, `duct_ids = E1` (one duct named for three sets). The E-621 DXF abbreviation note itself says "DUCTS = ... ONE DUCT PER SET", yet the F-05 row has one ID for three sets.
- `calc_book.xlsx`, sheet `duct_assignment`: only 9 rows — SE-1 sets 1-6, F-10 sets 1-2, and **F-05 set 1 only** (`E1`). Sets 2 and 3 of F-05 have no row.
- `design_basis.md`, JSON `duct_assignment`: `"F-05": ["E1"]`; prose §6: "F-05: one set in E1 (alone in DB-2, so no mutual heating)." The same one-set statement is in the author's summary. The design basis contradicts itself: §4 correctly says "F-05 runs **three parallel sets** of 600 kcmil aluminium", while §6 assigns one set to one duct.
- The cost ledger and voltage-drop calculation, by contrast, use **three** F-05 sets (600 kcmil AL: 6,444 ft = 3 sets × 3 phases × 716 ft; six 600 kcmil terminations; 2,148 ft of 3/0 EGC = 3 × 716).

**What it should be.** F-05 needs three ducts, one per set. DB-2 has three available ducts (E1, E2, E3; E4 is reserved for communications, E-619). `duct_ids` should read `E1,E2,E3`; `duct_assignment` should have rows F-05 set 1 → E1, set 2 → E2, set 3 → E3; the design-basis JSON/prose and the mutual-heating value for F-05 must reflect three loaded ducts (not "alone"/0 K).

**Evidence / consequence.** If the only named duct E1 is used for all three sets, 9 × 600 kcmil AL conductors (OD 0.948 in, area 0.7058 in² each) occupy 6.352 in² of a 4-in EPC-40 duct (internal area 12.730 in²) = **49.9 % fill, above the 40 % limit of EDS-26 6.1**, and three sets share one duct contrary to EDS-26 6.2. Under the task's scoring rule, "a cheap package that fails any of its hard families keeps none of [O′]"; this hard-family failure therefore withholds the package's entire installed-cost credit, not just F-05's. If the other two sets are placed elsewhere, the deliverable does not say where — a constructability and register failure. My EDS-26 5.3 calculation with the three F-05 sets in E1/E2/E3 gives dT ≈ 1.50 K and 399.9 A per set; the 75 °C termination cap of 336 A still governs, so the 336 A selection itself remains valid — but the hard-family duct assignment is not satisfied. Register R0121 ("one duct per set; ten ducts used in DB-1 and one in DB-2, no duct shared") and R0122 ("Applied in the duct assignment") are therefore false: DB-1 uses **8** loaded ducts (SE-1 6 + F-10 2), and DB-2 should use **3**, not one.


---

## 2. MAJOR — B-08 is declared at 45 °C; M-501-C requires 40 °C for that circuit

**Requirement.** M-501-C ambient table: ceiling cavity/return plenum = 40 °C; the 45 °C row applies to "every circuit whose whole run is inside [mechanical room 121 and fire pump room 105], and the feeders entering them: MCC-1, the fire pump, and the motor branch circuits fed from MCC-1." M-501-C note 3: every circuit routed on E-611/E-612/E-616 other than those named in the 45 °C row takes the ceiling-cavity 40 °C. EDS-26 5.2 requires the ambient of the space the raceway passes through from M-501-C.

**What the deliverable has.** `wire_schedule.csv`, B-08: `ambient_c = 45.0`; DXF B-08 `AMB C` 45.0. B-08 is fed from **LP-1** to KEF-1 and is routed on E-611; it is not MCC-1, the fire pump, or a motor branch fed from MCC-1. The author's own register agrees: R0133 (40 °C) lists B-08 and R0128 (45 °C) does not.

**What it should be.** 40 °C. The 90 °C ampacity at 40 °C is 54 × 0.9129 = 49.3 A; the governing 60 °C termination cap is 40 A either way, so the 8 AWG selection is still adequate, but the declared ambient and the hard ambient family for B-08 are wrong and conflict with the register.

**Evidence.** M-501-C p.1 rows and note 3; connected load schedule B-08 (from LP-1, routed E-611); `constraint_register.xlsx` R0128/R0133; `wire_schedule.csv` row B-08. This is the only circuit whose schedule ambient contradicts the memo. The conductor is safe either way, but if the verifier checks the declared `ambient_c` against M-501-C, B-08's hard ambient family fails and the package O′ is withheld under the same rule.


---

## 3. MAJOR (register precision / false hard-row) — R0012 applies the "not less than the branch device rating" rule to B-17, a motor feeder whose 6 AWG ampacity (54 A) is below its 60 A OCPD

**Requirement.** EDS-26 2.1: "Branch-circuit conductors supplying **lighting, receptacle and hard-wired appliance loads** are sized for not less than the rating of the branch device." EDS-26 2.1.1: for a motor, an A/C unit, an ASD, an elevator, a fire pump or a transformer "the conductor is sized on the load alone ... and the device rating is **NOT** a floor." NFPA 70 430.22/430.52 permit a motor branch OCPD above the conductor ampacity.

**What the deliverable has.** `constraint_register.xlsx` R0012 is HARD, text as above, with `applies_to = "B-01 to B-10, B-16 to B-18"` and resolution "Design current = branch device rating: 20, 40, 60, 100 A". B-17 is a motor feeder (shop air compressor CMP-1, 15 hp, motor schedule; connected-load class "Motor feeder"), OCPD 60 A, 125 % FLA design current 43.25 A, 6 AWG with 60 °C ampacity 54 A. B-08 is also a motor feeder (KEF-1, 5 hp), 30 A OCPD, design 17.75 A, 8 AWG 40 A.

**What it should be.** R0012 should apply only to the lighting, receptacle and hard-wired appliance circuits (B-01 to B-07, B-09, B-10, B-16, B-18), not to B-08 or B-17; those are governed by R0013/EDS-26 2.1.1, and B-17's 54 A < 60 A is expressly permitted for a motor branch (430.22/430.52; the overload, not the branch OCPD, protects the conductor). As written, the register contains a HARD row that lists B-17 and is numerically unsatisfied, which is exactly the "registered but not satisfied" condition the task penalises. The schedule itself is compliant: B-17 `design_current_a = 43.25`, `corrected_ampacity_a = 54`, `ocpd_a = 60`, and its `governing_constraint` correctly says ampacity/termination (not the device floor). The register resolution's "20, 40, 60, 100 A" also omits B-08's 30 A and misstates B-08/B-17 design currents.

**Evidence.** register R0012 and R0013; EDS-26 2.1 and 2.1.1; connected load schedule B-17 (OCPD 60, load 34.6); motor schedule CMP-1 (15 hp, 34.6 FLA); `wire_schedule.csv` B-17 (6 CU, amp 54, OCPD 60, design 43.25). If the verifier applies R0012 as written to B-17, this HARD row is registered but not satisfied (54 A < 60 A), so B-17's h would fail and the package O′ would be withheld; the correct fix is to remove B-08/B-17 from R0012's `applies_to`.


---

## 4. MAJOR — The service-entrance "not reducible" conclusion is wrong: five 600 kcmil Cu sets are feasible and about $1,262 cheaper

**Requirement.** Task.md §1: "minimise the installed cost of the conductor package"; EDS-26 8: "where two compliant selections exist, the lower installed cost governs." EDS-26 2.2/UFC 3-501-01 3-2.3.3 require SE-1 ampacity ≥ 2000 A (MSB-1 bus).

**What the deliverable has.** SE-1 = 6 sets × 500 kcmil Cu, 6 × 371.5 = 2,229 A. Design basis §5: "This is the largest single cost of the package and it is not reducible: five sets of 600 kcmil carry only 2064 A and cost more, and six sets of 400 kcmil reach only 1993 A once mutual heating is included."

**What it should be.** Five 600 kcmil Cu sets in the best available DB-1 positions (D1, D2, D3, D9, D10, with F-10 in D4, D8) give, by the EDS-26 5.3 Neher-McGrath calculation with the same loads (SE-1 1732/5 = 346.4 A per set; F-10 432/2 = 216 A per duct), a minimum set ampacity of **403.7 A** → **2,018.5 A ≥ 2,000 A** (the D2 set is the limiting one; the other sets are 406.0–420.3 A). 600 kcmil Cu is already one of the five standard sizes (F-05 uses 600 kcmil Al), 5 ≤ 6 terminals, and 600 ≤ 600 kcmil terminal max at T-1/MSB-1. Fill in a 5-in duct is 10.6 % and jam ratio 5.32, both compliant.

**Cost evidence (Cascadia price list, 6 % quantity break):** 6 × 500 Cu: phase 5,760 ft × $6.25 = $36,000.00; 4/0 EGC 1,920 ft × $2.876 = $5,521.92; 500 kcmil terminations 12 × $193 = $2,316.00; gross $43,837.92. 5 × 600 Cu: phase 4,800 ft × $7.42 = $35,616.00; EGC 1,600 ft × $2.876 = $4,601.60; 600 kcmil terminations 10 × $228 = $2,280.00; gross $42,497.60. Net of the 6 % conductor break the saving is **≈ $1,262** (total length still 39,752 ft ≥ 38,000 ft). The design basis's "2064 A" is not reproducible from the EDS-26 5.3 calculation (the loaded best arrangement gives 2018.5 A) and the "cost more" claim is arithmetically false; the selected 6 × 500 is compliant but **not** cost-minimal. **Caveat:** the 5 × 600 option raises SE-1's own drop from 1.043 % to 1.1225 % (R 0.0240 vs 0.0278, 5 sets vs 6), so B-17's cumulative becomes 5.0075 % — above the nominal 5.0 % but inside the task's 0.02 percentage-point allowance; the author's 6 × 500 (4.928 %) has more margin. The alternative is therefore feasible within the stated tolerance, but tight on both ampacity (2018.5 A vs 2000 A) and voltage drop.

**Evidence.** My script implementing EDS-26 5.3 (all geometry from E-619; Rac(Tc) from Cascadia 4.1; dT_m at connected load/sets) reproduces the author's 371.5 A for 6 × 500 and gives 403.7 A min for 5 × 600 in D1/D2/D3/D9/D10. Price list rows 500/600 kcmil; ledger lines for SE-1.

## 5. MAJOR — Register row R0111 states F-05's EGC as 2/0, which would not satisfy NFPA 70 250.122(B); the schedule/ledger use 3/0

**Requirement.** EDS-26 5.7 / NFPA 70 250.122(B): where the phase conductor is increased above the ampacity-only size, increase the EGC in the same circular-mil ratio. The "ampacity-only" size is the smallest **admissible** size under EDS-26 3.2, 3.3 and **3.4** — i.e. one of the five standard sizes. For F-05 the smallest standard size meeting 400 A (3 sets, 133.3 A/set) is **4/0** (211,600 cmil), not 250 kcmil (250 kcmil is not one of the five sizes and is not admissible under 3.4.2).

**What the deliverable has.** `constraint_register.xlsx` R0111 resolution: "F-05 600 kcmil against a 250 kcmil ampacity minimum gives a 2/0 EGC." The schedule and ledger actually use **3/0** (167,806 cmil) for F-05.

**What it should be.** Base EGC for 400 A = 3 AWG (52,635 cmil); ratio 600,000/211,600 = 2.8356; 52,635 × 2.8356 = 149,245 cmil → next standard size **3/0** (167,806). A 2/0 EGC (133,077 cmil) is below 149,245 and would be undersized. The schedule's 3/0 is correct; the register's resolution is wrong and contradicts the design. R0111 also lists F-01 and F-07, whose phases were not increased for VD (500 Al is the ampacity-only standard size), so those applies_to entries are over-broad.

**Evidence.** EDS-26 5.7; `wire_schedule.csv` F-05 `egc_size = 3/0`; ledger "Equipment grounding conductor, Cu, 3/0" 2,148 ft = 3 × 716; register R0111.


---

## 6. MINOR — B-08 EGC is one size larger than 250.122(B) requires (4 AWG vs 6 AWG)

**Requirement.** EDS-26 5.7 / NFPA 70 250.122(B). B-08: OCPD 30 A → base EGC 10 AWG (10,383 cmil); ampacity-only phase at 17.75 A is 12 AWG (6,530 cmil, 60 °C 22 A); actual phase 8 AWG (16,510 cmil); ratio 2.528 → 10,383 × 2.528 = 26,251 cmil = **6 AWG**. The schedule uses 4 AWG (41,741 cmil).

**What it should be.** 6 AWG. The over-size is not a safety violation, but it costs about $37 on 207 ft and contradicts the design basis's claim that EGCs are increased "in the same circular-mil ratio". Evidence: `wire_schedule.csv` B-08; Cascadia/250.122 table.

## 7. MINOR — Ledger material + labour does not equal the ledger total (2-cent rounding mismatch)

**Requirement.** Task.md §3 `cost_ledger`: each line "showing its material and its labour content"; task.md grading: "where the ledger shows material and labour they must add up to it." `total_usd` must equal the ledger total.

**What the deliverable has.** `calc_book.xlsx` `cost_ledger` Total row: material 99,091.34 + labour 53,407.03 = **152,498.37**, but `amount_usd` = **152,498.35** (also `front_sheet.total_usd` 152,498.35 and design_basis `total_usd` 152,498.35). Six individual lines also have 1-cent material+labor vs amount differences: 12 Cu 34.44+40.76=75.20 vs 75.21; EGC 8 874.68 vs 874.67; EGC 3 1,424.44 vs 1,424.43; EGC 1/0 622.94 vs 622.93; EGC 3/0 5,075.73 vs 5,075.72; adjustment -6,061.34 vs -6,061.33.

**What it should be.** One consistent set of rounded line amounts and a Total whose material + labour equals its amount (and `total_usd`). The 2-cent difference is rounding, but the arithmetic identity the task asks for does not hold. Evidence: scripted sum of the `cost_ledger` columns.

## 8. MINOR — Tray circuits report `ccc = 3`, but the design used N = 18 current-carrying conductors in CT-R1

**Requirement.** Task.md §1: `ccc` is "the number of current-carrying conductors the design assumed for this circuit." EDS-26 5.4: k_t = 1 + 0.06(N − 3), N = current-carrying conductors **in the tray**.

**What the deliverable has.** F-04, F-08, F-12, F-13: `ccc = 3` in both CSV and DXF; `calc_book.front_sheet` has `tray_current_carrying_conductors = 18`; the ampacity 171.9 A is computed with k_t = 1.9 (N = 18). The declared per-circuit column therefore does not state the grouping actually assumed for the tray ampacity.

**What it should be.** 18 (or an explicit note that 3 is per set and 18 in the tray). Evidence: `calc_book` row; EDS-26 5.4; my recomputation of 4/0 Al at 46 °C, k_t = 1.9 gives 171.9 A.

## 9. MINOR — `governing_constraint` names non-binding or omits binding requirements on several circuits

**Requirement.** Task.md §1: "`governing_constraint` names ... the requirement or requirements that decided this conductor's size. More than one can bind at once; name the ones that did."

**What the deliverable has / should be.**
- **B-09** says ampacity/termination only. A 6 AWG would fail both: 60 °C ampacity 54 A < 60 A and its own VD would be 3.26 % (cumulative 6.07 % > 5 %). VD also binds.
- **B-17** says ampacity/termination only. An 8 AWG would fail ampacity (40 A < 43.25 A) and VD (3.66 % own, cumulative 6.24 % > 5 %). VD also binds.
- **F-07** says ampacity/termination only. Three 350 kcmil Al sets would fail ampacity (774 A < 780.67 A) **and** VD (1.94 % own, cumulative 3.34 % > 3 %). VD also binds.
- **F-10** says "+ voltage drop". A 300 kcmil Cu set is excluded by the 75 °C termination cap (295 A < 300 A); its VD (1.91 % own, cumulative 2.96 %) would pass. VD did not decide the size.

- **F-01** is correctly shown as ampacity/termination only: two 350 kcmil Al sets fail ampacity (504 A < 600 A) but their VD is 1.92 % own / 2.96 % cumulative, inside the 3 % feeder limit. No change needed.

These are declaration errors, not conductor-selection errors. Evidence: the CSV's own lengths/R/X and the next-smaller standard-size checks.

## 10. MINOR — Register R0162 cites EDS-26 3.4.4 for parallel-conductor sameness; that requirement is in Section 26 05 19 3.1

**Requirement.** Section 26 05 19 3.1: "Conductors in parallel must be of the same length, material, size, insulation and termination method, and each set must be installed in its own raceway or duct." Register R0040 already cites the correct 26 05 19 3.1 row; R0162 duplicates it with the wrong clause. Evidence: EDS-26 Rev 4 3.4.4; Section 26 05 19 3.1; register R0040/R0162.

## 11. MINOR — Register R0028 omits F-06 from the aluminium applies_to list and misstates the size range

**Requirement.** UFC 3-520-01 3-6.3.1 / EDS-26 3.2: aluminium may be used for #4 AWG and larger. F-06 is 4/0 Al (one of the nine aluminium circuits in the schedule and design basis). R0028 applies_to is "F-01,F-04,F-05,F-07 to F-09,F-12,F-13" — F-06 is missing. Its resolution says "250 to 600 kcmil", but 4/0 is 211.6 kcmil and is used on F-04, F-06, F-08, F-12, F-13. # Independent review — LV cable sizing, Building 4210 (P-4210)

Scope reviewed: `/filesystem/electrical__lv_cable_sizing__blind/output/submission.zip` (5 files), against task.md, EDS-26 Rev 4, G-001, UFC 3-501-01, UFC 3-520-01, M-501-C, GEO-4210-T, E-619/E-618/E-611/E-612/E-613/E-615/E-616, the schedules, Cascadia data/price list and the unit price book. I re-derived lengths, ampacities, voltage drops, duct temperatures, EGCs and the ledger from the source documents; I did not reuse the author's scripts. Findings are most serious first.

---

## 1. BLOCKING — F-05 has three parallel sets but only one duct is assigned; the duct assignment is incomplete and, as documented, violates the one-set-per-duct and 40 % fill rules

**Requirement.** Task.md §1 (`duct_ids` "names the duct each set occupies, for duct-bank circuits only"); task.md §3 `duct_assignment` "one row per parallel set of each duct-bank circuit"; EDS-26 Rev 4 6.2 "One three-phase set occupies one duct; a duct must not carry conductors of more than one circuit"; EDS-26 6.1 40 % fill; Section 26 05 33 3.2 "One three-phase circuit per duct." The task's 25 hard families explicitly include "the duct assignment in the design basis".

**What the deliverable has.**
- `wire_schedule.csv`, circuit F-05: `sets = 3`, `size = 600 kcmil`, `material = AL`, `duct_ids = E1` (one duct named for three sets). The E-621 DXF abbreviation note itself says "DUCTS = ... ONE DUCT PER SET", yet the F-05 row has one ID for three sets.
- `calc_book.xlsx`, sheet `duct_assignment`: only 9 rows — SE-1 sets 1-6, F-10 sets 1-2, and **F-05 set 1 only** (`E1`). Sets 2 and 3 of F-05 have no row.
- `design_basis.md`, JSON `duct_assignment`: `"F-05": ["E1"]`; prose §6: "F-05: one set in E1 (alone in DB-2, so no mutual heating)." The same one-set statement is in the author's summary. The design basis contradicts itself: §4 correctly says "F-05 runs **three parallel sets** of 600 kcmil aluminium", while §6 assigns one set to one duct.
- The cost ledger and voltage-drop calculation, by contrast, use **three** F-05 sets (600 kcmil AL: 6,444 ft = 3 sets × 3 phases × 716 ft; six 600 kcmil terminations; 2,148 ft of 3/0 EGC = 3 × 716).

**What it should be.** F-05 needs three ducts, one per set. DB-2 has three available ducts (E1, E2, E3; E4 is reserved for communications, E-619). `duct_ids` should read `E1,E2,E3`; `duct_assignment` should have rows F-05 set 1 → E1, set 2 → E2, set 3 → E3; the design-basis JSON/prose and the mutual-heating value for F-05 must reflect three loaded ducts (not "alone"/0 K).

**Evidence / consequence.** If the only named duct E1 is used for all three sets, 9 × 600 kcmil AL conductors (OD 0.948 in, area 0.7058 in² each) occupy 6.352 in² of a 4-in EPC-40 duct (internal area 12.730 in²) = **49.9 % fill, above the 40 % limit of EDS-26 6.1**, and three sets share one duct contrary to EDS-26 6.2. Under the task's scoring rule, "a cheap package that fails any of its hard families keeps none of [O′]"; this hard-family failure therefore withholds the package's entire installed-cost credit, not just F-05's. If the other two sets are placed elsewhere, the deliverable does not say where — a constructability and register failure. My EDS-26 5.3 calculation with the three F-05 sets in E1/E2/E3 gives dT ≈ 1.50 K and 399.9 A per set; the 75 °C termination cap of 336 A still governs, so the 336 A selection itself remains valid — but the hard-family duct assignment is not satisfied. Register R0121 ("one duct per set; ten ducts used in DB-1 and one in DB-2, no duct shared") and R0122 ("Applied in the duct assignment") are therefore false: DB-1 uses **8** loaded ducts (SE-1 6 + F-10 2), and DB-2 should use **3**, not one.


---

## 2. MAJOR — B-08 is declared at 45 °C; M-501-C requires 40 °C for that circuit

**Requirement.** M-501-C ambient table: ceiling cavity/return plenum = 40 °C; the 45 °C row applies to "every circuit whose whole run is inside [mechanical room 121 and fire pump room 105], and the feeders entering them: MCC-1, the fire pump, and the motor branch circuits fed from MCC-1." M-501-C note 3: every circuit routed on E-611/E-612/E-616 other than those named in the 45 °C row takes the ceiling-cavity 40 °C. EDS-26 5.2 requires the ambient of the space the raceway passes through from M-501-C.

**What the deliverable has.** `wire_schedule.csv`, B-08: `ambient_c = 45.0`; DXF B-08 `AMB C` 45.0. B-08 is fed from **LP-1** to KEF-1 and is routed on E-611; it is not MCC-1, the fire pump, or a motor branch fed from MCC-1. The author's own register agrees: R0133 (40 °C) lists B-08 and R0128 (45 °C) does not.

**What it should be.** 40 °C. The 90 °C ampacity at 40 °C is 54 × 0.9129 = 49.3 A; the governing 60 °C termination cap is 40 A either way, so the 8 AWG selection is still adequate, but the declared ambient and the hard ambient family for B-08 are wrong and conflict with the register.

**Evidence.** M-501-C p.1 rows and note 3; connected load schedule B-08 (from LP-1, routed E-611); `constraint_register.xlsx` R0128/R0133; `wire_schedule.csv` row B-08. This is the only circuit whose schedule ambient contradicts the memo. The conductor is safe either way, but if the verifier checks the declared `ambient_c` against M-501-C, B-08's hard ambient family fails and the package O′ is withheld under the same rule.


---

## 3. MAJOR (register precision / false hard-row) — R0012 applies the "not less than the branch device rating" rule to B-17, a motor feeder whose 6 AWG ampacity (54 A) is below its 60 A OCPD

**Requirement.** EDS-26 2.1: "Branch-circuit conductors supplying **lighting, receptacle and hard-wired appliance loads** are sized for not less than the rating of the branch device." EDS-26 2.1.1: for a motor, an A/C unit, an ASD, an elevator, a fire pump or a transformer "the conductor is sized on the load alone ... and the device rating is **NOT** a floor." NFPA 70 430.22/430.52 permit a motor branch OCPD above the conductor ampacity.

**What the deliverable has.** `constraint_register.xlsx` R0012 is HARD, text as above, with `applies_to = "B-01 to B-10, B-16 to B-18"` and resolution "Design current = branch device rating: 20, 40, 60, 100 A". B-17 is a motor feeder (shop air compressor CMP-1, 15 hp, motor schedule; connected-load class "Motor feeder"), OCPD 60 A, 125 % FLA design current 43.25 A, 6 AWG with 60 °C ampacity 54 A. B-08 is also a motor feeder (KEF-1, 5 hp), 30 A OCPD, design 17.75 A, 8 AWG 40 A.

**What it should be.** R0012 should apply only to the lighting, receptacle and hard-wired appliance circuits (B-01 to B-07, B-09, B-10, B-16, B-18), not to B-08 or B-17; those are governed by R0013/EDS-26 2.1.1, and B-17's 54 A < 60 A is expressly permitted for a motor branch (430.22/430.52; the overload, not the branch OCPD, protects the conductor). As written, the register contains a HARD row that lists B-17 and is numerically unsatisfied, which is exactly the "registered but not satisfied" condition the task penalises. The schedule itself is compliant: B-17 `design_current_a = 43.25`, `corrected_ampacity_a = 54`, `ocpd_a = 60`, and its `governing_constraint` correctly says ampacity/termination (not the device floor). The register resolution's "20, 40, 60, 100 A" also omits B-08's 30 A and misstates B-08/B-17 design currents.

**Evidence.** register R0012 and R0013; EDS-26 2.1 and 2.1.1; connected load schedule B-17 (OCPD 60, load 34.6); motor schedule CMP-1 (15 hp, 34.6 FLA); `wire_schedule.csv` B-17 (6 CU, amp 54, OCPD 60, design 43.25). If the verifier applies R0012 as written to B-17, this HARD row is registered but not satisfied (54 A < 60 A), so B-17's h would fail and the package O′ would be withheld; the correct fix is to remove B-08/B-17 from R0012's `applies_to`.


---

## 4. MAJOR — The service-entrance "not reducible" conclusion is wrong: five 600 kcmil Cu sets are feasible and about $1,262 cheaper

**Requirement.** Task.md §1: "minimise the installed cost of the conductor package"; EDS-26 8: "where two compliant selections exist, the lower installed cost governs." EDS-26 2.2/UFC 3-501-01 3-2.3.3 require SE-1 ampacity ≥ 2000 A (MSB-1 bus).

**What the deliverable has.** SE-1 = 6 sets × 500 kcmil Cu, 6 × 371.5 = 2,229 A. Design basis §5: "This is the largest single cost of the package and it is not reducible: five sets of 600 kcmil carry only 2064 A and cost more, and six sets of 400 kcmil reach only 1993 A once mutual heating is included."

**What it should be.** Five 600 kcmil Cu sets in the best available DB-1 positions (D1, D2, D3, D9, D10, with F-10 in D4, D8) give, by the EDS-26 5.3 Neher-McGrath calculation with the same loads (SE-1 1732/5 = 346.4 A per set; F-10 432/2 = 216 A per duct), a minimum set ampacity of **403.7 A** → **2,018.5 A ≥ 2,000 A** (the D2 set is the limiting one; the other sets are 406.0–420.3 A). 600 kcmil Cu is already one of the five standard sizes (F-05 uses 600 kcmil Al), 5 ≤ 6 terminals, and 600 ≤ 600 kcmil terminal max at T-1/MSB-1. Fill in a 5-in duct is 10.6 % and jam ratio 5.32, both compliant.

**Cost evidence (Cascadia price list, 6 % quantity break):** 6 × 500 Cu: phase 5,760 ft × $6.25 = $36,000.00; 4/0 EGC 1,920 ft × $2.876 = $5,521.92; 500 kcmil terminations 12 × $193 = $2,316.00; gross $43,837.92. 5 × 600 Cu: phase 4,800 ft × $7.42 = $35,616.00; EGC 1,600 ft × $2.876 = $4,601.60; 600 kcmil terminations 10 × $228 = $2,280.00; gross $42,497.60. Net of the 6 % conductor break the saving is **≈ $1,262** (total length still 39,752 ft ≥ 38,000 ft). The design basis's "2064 A" is not reproducible from the EDS-26 5.3 calculation (the loaded best arrangement gives 2018.5 A) and the "cost more" claim is arithmetically false; the selected 6 × 500 is compliant but **not** cost-minimal. **Caveat:** the 5 × 600 option raises SE-1's own drop from 1.043 % to 1.1225 % (R 0.0240 vs 0.0278, 5 sets vs 6), so B-17's cumulative becomes 5.0075 % — above the nominal 5.0 % but inside the task's 0.02 percentage-point allowance; the author's 6 × 500 (4.928 %) has more margin. The alternative is therefore feasible within the stated tolerance, but tight on both ampacity (2018.5 A vs 2000 A) and voltage drop.

**Evidence.** My script implementing EDS-26 5.3 (all geometry from E-619; Rac(Tc) from Cascadia 4.1; dT_m at connected load/sets) reproduces the author's 371.5 A for 6 × 500 and gives 403.7 A min for 5 × 600 in D1/D2/D3/D9/D10. Price list rows 500/600 kcmil; ledger lines for SE-1.


---

## 5. MAJOR — Register row R0111 states F-05's EGC as 2/0, which would not satisfy NFPA 70 250.122(B); the schedule/ledger use 3/0

**Requirement.** EDS-26 5.7 / NFPA 70 250.122(B): where the phase conductor is increased above the ampacity-only size, increase the EGC in the same circular-mil ratio. The "ampacity-only" size is the smallest **admissible** size under EDS-26 3.2, 3.3 and **3.4** — i.e. one of the five standard sizes. For F-05 the smallest standard size meeting 400 A (3 sets, 133.3 A/set) is **4/0** (211,600 cmil), not 250 kcmil (250 kcmil is not one of the five sizes and is not admissible under 3.4.2).

**What the deliverable has.** `constraint_register.xlsx` R0111 resolution: "F-05 600 kcmil against a 250 kcmil ampacity minimum gives a 2/0 EGC." The schedule and ledger actually use **3/0** (167,806 cmil) for F-05.

**What it should be.** Base EGC for 400 A = 3 AWG (52,635 cmil); ratio 600,000/211,600 = 2.8356; 52,635 × 2.8356 = 149,245 cmil → next standard size **3/0** (167,806). A 2/0 EGC (133,077 cmil) is below 149,245 and would be undersized. The schedule's 3/0 is correct; the register's resolution is wrong and contradicts the design. R0111 also lists F-01 and F-07, whose phases were not increased for VD (500 Al is the ampacity-only standard size), so those applies_to entries are over-broad.

**Evidence.** EDS-26 5.7; `wire_schedule.csv` F-05 `egc_size = 3/0`; ledger "Equipment grounding conductor, Cu, 3/0" 2,148 ft = 3 × 716; register R0111.


---

## 6. MINOR — B-08 EGC is one size larger than 250.122(B) requires (4 AWG vs 6 AWG)

**Requirement.** EDS-26 5.7 / NFPA 70 250.122(B). B-08: OCPD 30 A → base EGC 10 AWG (10,383 cmil); ampacity-only phase at 17.75 A is 12 AWG (6,530 cmil, 60 °C 22 A); actual phase 8 AWG (16,510 cmil); ratio 2.528 → 10,383 × 2.528 = 26,251 cmil = **6 AWG**. The schedule uses 4 AWG (41,741 cmil).

**What it should be.** 6 AWG. The over-size is not a safety violation, but it costs about $37 on 207 ft and contradicts the design basis's claim that EGCs are increased "in the same circular-mil ratio". Evidence: `wire_schedule.csv` B-08; Cascadia/250.122 table.

## 7. MINOR — Ledger material + labour does not equal the ledger total (2-cent rounding mismatch)

**Requirement.** Task.md §3 `cost_ledger`: each line "showing its material and its labour content"; task.md grading: "where the ledger shows material and labour they must add up to it." `total_usd` must equal the ledger total.

**What the deliverable has.** `calc_book.xlsx` `cost_ledger` Total row: material 99,091.34 + labour 53,407.03 = **152,498.37**, but `amount_usd` = **152,498.35** (also `front_sheet.total_usd` 152,498.35 and design_basis `total_usd` 152,498.35). Six individual lines also have 1-cent material+labor vs amount differences: 12 Cu 34.44+40.76=75.20 vs 75.21; EGC 8 874.68 vs 874.67; EGC 3 1,424.44 vs 1,424.43; EGC 1/0 622.94 vs 622.93; EGC 3/0 5,075.73 vs 5,075.72; adjustment -6,061.34 vs -6,061.33.

**What it should be.** One consistent set of rounded line amounts and a Total whose material + labour equals its amount (and `total_usd`). The 2-cent difference is rounding, but the arithmetic identity the task asks for does not hold. Evidence: scripted sum of the `cost_ledger` columns.

## 8. MINOR — Tray circuits report `ccc = 3`, but the design used N = 18 current-carrying conductors in CT-R1

**Requirement.** Task.md §1: `ccc` is "the number of current-carrying conductors the design assumed for this circuit." EDS-26 5.4: k_t = 1 + 0.06(N − 3), N = current-carrying conductors **in the tray**.

**What the deliverable has.** F-04, F-08, F-12, F-13: `ccc = 3` in both CSV and DXF; `calc_book.front_sheet` has `tray_current_carrying_conductors = 18`; the ampacity 171.9 A is computed with k_t = 1.9 (N = 18). The declared per-circuit column therefore does not state the grouping actually assumed for the tray ampacity.

**What it should be.** 18 (or an explicit note that 3 is per set and 18 in the tray). Evidence: `calc_book` row; EDS-26 5.4; my recomputation of 4/0 Al at 46 °C, k_t = 1.9 gives 171.9 A.

## 9. MINOR — `governing_constraint` names non-binding or omits binding requirements on several circuits

**Requirement.** Task.md §1: "`governing_constraint` names ... the requirement or requirements that decided this conductor's size. More than one can bind at once; name the ones that did."

**What the deliverable has / should be.**
- **B-09** says ampacity/termination only. A 6 AWG would fail both: 60 °C ampacity 54 A < 60 A and its own VD would be 3.26 % (cumulative 6.07 % > 5 %). VD also binds.

These are declaration errors, not conductor-selection errors. Evidence: the CSV's own lengths/R/X and the next-smaller standard-size checks.

## 19. MINOR — Register R0163 and design_basis §9 cite UFC 3-501-01 "2-2.c"; the NESC/IEEE C2 clause is 2-1.11.c

**Requirement.** The clause that says "Design all exterior underground and overhead, medium, and low voltage systems not specifically associated with a building/support structure in accordance with the general requirements of IEEE C2 except utilize the NFPA 70 ampacity and conduit fill tables for all designs" is UFC 3-501-01 **2-1.11.c** (NFPA 70 / IEEE C2 Design Interface Points), not 2-2.c. UFC 3-501-01 2-2 is "Site Exterior Power Distribution Systems" and 2-2.3 is exterior lighting; there is no 2-2.c.

**What the deliverable has.** `constraint_register.xlsx` R0163 `clause = 2-2.c`; `design_basis.md` §9 table row "UFC 3-501-01 2-2.c directs NFPA 70 ampacity tables for exterior systems". The substantive conclusion (the clause is limited to exterior systems not associated with a building, so it does not override EDS-26 5.1 for the Building 4210 service laterals) is correct, but the citation is wrong.

**What it should be.** 2-1.11.c. Evidence: UFC 3-501-01 text at 2-1.11.c; register R0163; design_basis §9.

# Low-voltage wire schedule — Building 4210, Consolidated Support Facility

This brief has two parts. **Engineering brief** is the job, as the engineer of record would
receive it. **Benchmark submission requirements** says how the package is filed and scored here;
it is scaffolding of this benchmark, not part of a real project.

# Part 1 — Engineering brief

You are the electrical engineer of record for a new consolidated support facility at a naval
installation. The project data room — the folder of project documents issued to the design
team — is in `project/`: the governing federal criteria in `criteria/`, the installation's own
electrical design standard in `owner/` (with the superseded revision alongside it), the contract
specifications in `specs/`, the issued-for-construction drawing set in `drawings/`, the
equipment, connected-load and motor schedules in `schedules/`, the site investigation, climate
record, coordination memoranda and the utility's service letter in `site/`, the cable
engineering data and price list in `vendor/`, and the unit price book in `procurement/`.

The one-line series is drawn, the equipment is procured and released for manufacture, and the
overcurrent devices are set. **What is missing is the wire.** Specify the type, material and
size of every low-voltage feeder and branch circuit in the scope, using parallel sets when
necessary, the equipment grounding conductor, the raceway and — for the circuits that run
underground — the ductbanks, as well. Publish the result as the wire schedule sheet of the
E-600 series, and **minimise the installed cost of the conductor package** while satisfying
every requirement the data room imposes, including the codes of record the project was
designed under.

Nothing in this brief tells you a design value, a limit, a formula or a temperature. Every
number you need — the ampacity model and its constants, the corrections, the thermal properties
of the ground, the ambient temperatures, the voltage-drop limits and the load each class of
circuit is calculated at, the termination ratings, the routing and length rules, the
standardisation and procurement limits, the codes of record and their editions, and the
prices — is in the documents, and finding which document carries which is part of the work.
Circuit lengths are not tabulated anywhere: they are measured from the plans and the riser
diagram. Where two documents disagree, or where one has been superseded, the data room says
which governs, and your design basis has to say what you resolved and why.

The circuits are not decided independently of one another. They share a voltage-drop budget
along each path from the source, they share the thermal environment of a duct bank and of a
roof cable tray.

## Deliverables

Five files.

### 1. `wire_schedule.csv`

One row per circuit, every circuit in the connected load schedule, 32 rows. Columns, exactly
these names:

```
circuit, description, from, to, install_class, length_ft, sets, size, material, egc_size,
raceway_trade_in, duct_ids, design_current_a, corrected_ampacity_a, vd_load_a, vd_pct,
cumulative_vd_pct, ambient_c, ccc, governing_constraint, ocpd_a, system_voltage_v, phases,
power_factor, r_ohm_per_kft, x_ohm_per_kft, drop_v
```

* `size` and `egc_size` are trade sizes: `12`, `10`, `8`, `6`, `4`, `3`, `2`, `1`, `1/0`, `2/0`,
  `3/0`, `4/0`, `250 kcmil` … `750 kcmil`. `material` is `CU` or `AL`.
* `length_ft` is the length your calculation used. `sets` is the number of parallel sets.
* `raceway_trade_in` is the conduit trade size in inches, for circuits in interior raceway only.
  `duct_ids` names the duct each set occupies, for duct-bank circuits only.
* `design_current_a` is the current the conductor's corrected ampacity had to carry;
  `corrected_ampacity_a` is the ampacity per set that your selection actually has after every
  correction, adjustment and limit; `vd_load_a` is the current your voltage-drop calculation
  used, which is not necessarily either of the other two.
* `vd_pct` is this circuit's own voltage drop; `cumulative_vd_pct` is the voltage drop at the
  load at the end of this circuit, counted from the calculation starting point. Voltage drop is
  not held to one number: feeders, branch circuits and the total at the load each have their
  own limit, and some equipment has limits of its own. Which limit applies to which circuit is
  set by the governing criteria in the data room.
* `ambient_c` and `ccc` are the ambient temperature and the number of current-carrying
  conductors the design assumed for this circuit.
* `governing_constraint` names, in your own words, the requirement or requirements that decided
  this conductor's size. More than one can bind at once; name the ones that did.
* The last seven columns let a reviewer audit the schedule. `ocpd_a` is the rating, in amperes,
  of the overcurrent protective device of the circuit. `system_voltage_v`, `phases`,
  `power_factor`, `r_ohm_per_kft` and `x_ohm_per_kft` (the conductor resistance and reactance per
  1000 ft) are the values your voltage-drop calculation used for this circuit, and `drop_v` is the
  circuit's own voltage drop in volts.

### 2. `E-621_wire_schedule.dxf`

The contract sheet. A DXF carrying a title block that names the project number and the sheet
number E-621, and the schedule itself: one line per circuit, starting with the circuit
designation, carrying the columns of `wire_schedule.csv` in the same order (abbreviated headers
and values are fine, with an abbreviation list on the sheet), and agreeing with
`wire_schedule.csv` on the circuit designation and the conductor size.

### 3. `calc_book.xlsx`

The calculation front sheet — the parameters your calculation stands on, so that a reviewer can
reproduce it. A workbook with exactly these three sheets, each with the header row shown as its
first row.

Sheet `front_sheet`:

```
parameter, value, unit, source_document, clause
```

one row per parameter, with at least these parameters:

```
outdoor_design_dry_bulb_c, roof_ambient_c, earth_ambient_c,
soil_thermal_resistivity_k_m_w, encasement_thermal_resistivity_k_m_w,
solar_irradiance_w_m2, load_factor, termination_allowance_ft, vd_start_point,
vd_limit_feeder_pct, vd_limit_branch_pct, vd_limit_total_pct, mutual_heating_rise_k,
tray_sum_od_in, distinct_large_sizes, ampacity_basis, total_usd
```

`ampacity_basis` states the basis of the ampacities used: the method, and the code article that
permits it. `soil_thermal_resistivity_k_m_w` is the resistivity your earth and mutual-heating
terms actually used; a value you considered and rejected goes in a row of its own. `source_document` and `clause` say where each value came from.

Sheet `duct_assignment`:

```
circuit, set, duct
```

one row per parallel set of each duct-bank circuit. Write duct identifiers as the duct-bank
sections label them.

Sheet `cost_ledger`:

```
line, quantity, unit, material_usd, labor_usd, amount_usd
```

your ledger — conductor, terminations and raceway, with any project-wide price adjustment as a
line of its own — at the project's own unit prices, each line showing its material and its
labour content, and a last row whose `line` is `Total`. `total_usd` on the front sheet is the
installed cost of the package and equals the ledger total.

### 4. `design_basis.md`

The engineering narrative, opening with a fenced ```json block carrying at least:

```
codes_of_record {nfpa70_edition, ibc_edition, adopted_by, precedence},
environment {outdoor_design_dry_bulb_c, roof_ambient_c, earth_ambient_c,
            soil_thermal_resistivity_k_m_w, solar_irradiance_w_m2},
sources     {which document each of those came from},
voltage_drop {start_point, transformer_reset, feeder_chain_pct, branch_limit_pct,
             total_limit_pct},
cost        {conductor_usd, termination_usd, raceway_usd, material_usd, labor_usd, total_usd},
duct_assignment, mutual_heating_rise_k
```

In that block `precedence` is the rule that decides between two criteria that set different
limits, `adopted_by` names the document that adopts the two codes, `transformer_reset` says
whether the voltage-drop count restarts at the low-voltage transformer, `feeder_chain_pct` is
the voltage drop your feeder chains actually spend (one number, or one per chain) and
`duct_assignment` maps each duct-bank circuit to the ducts its sets occupy.

and then the prose: the codes of record the design was prepared against, the document that
adopts them and the order of precedence among the criteria; the environmental parameters and
their provenance; how the voltage-drop budget was allocated along the chain, what the
starting point is, whether the count restarts at the low-voltage transformer and how many branch
circuits inherit the budget spent upstream of their panel; the service-entrance sizing decision; the duct-bank assignment, how many
ducts of the service duct bank were available to it, and its thermal consequence for the other
circuits in the bank; the material and standardisation
decisions; and the cost ledger, material and labour.

# Part 2 — Benchmark submission requirements

Write `output/submission.zip` (at most 25 MB and 200 files) containing the four files above and
the register below, five files at the top level.

### 5. `constraint_register.xlsx` — the code-compliance matrix

A federal Basis of Design carries a criteria log: the requirements the design was held to, each
traced to its document and clause. Here it is filed as a workbook and scored, because it is how
this benchmark tells a design that was engineered to a requirement from one that met it by
chance. One requirement per row, in a sheet whose header row carries exactly these columns:

```
req_id, document, clause, requirement, value, unit, kind, applies_to, resolution
```

`document` is the source document, `clause` its clause, table, section or sheet identifier,
`value` the number the requirement fixes where it fixes one, `kind` HARD or SOFT,
`applies_to` the circuits or the part of the package it binds, and `resolution` how you applied
it, including how you resolved any conflict. **One row states one requirement**: a row is
credited with at most one of them, and a row that cites several clauses at once, or carries a
list of unrelated values, is not a register row and counts against precision. Register the
requirements you actually engineered to: a requirement you satisfied but never registered does
not count as engineered, and a requirement you registered but did not satisfy does not either.
Rows that cite a superseded document, a document that is not in the data room, or a product
that is not the basis of design, as though it governed, reduce the register's precision —
unless the row itself says that the document does not govern. A national code that the data
room adopts by reference but does not contain may be cited by name and article; such a row is
neutral. Extra correct rows are neutral: a thorough register is never penalised for being long.
The first 400 rows are scanned and the precision floor is 0.6.

## How this is graded

Each of the circuits in the graded set is scored

```
score = 0.4 · p  +  0.6 · [h = 1] · O′
```

* `p` is the fraction of the 35 constraint families that are both **satisfied** for that circuit
  and **registered** in `constraint_register.xlsx`, scaled by `min(1, precision / 0.6)`.
* `h` is the fraction of the 25 hard families that are both satisfied and registered for that
  circuit (not scaled by precision); `[h = 1]` is 1 when all 25 are, else 0. A row that is missing or
  unreadable scores 0. The hard families include
  the declaration of the codes of record, the voltage-drop budget allocation and the duct
  assignment in the design basis, not only the conductor selections.
* `O′` is the credit for the installed cost of the package, measured against a certified lower
  bound on the cost of any compliant design and rescaled onto the band between a named naive
  baseline and a package cheaper than the reference design. A hard violation withholds it: a cheap
  package that fails any of its hard families keeps none of it. An incomplete package gains nothing
  either: a circuit left out of the schedule is charged at
  the naive baseline's cost for it.
* The cost that is scored is the one the grader recomputes from your own selections and the
  project's unit prices, not the one you declare — but the two must agree, and where the ledger
  shows material and labour they must add up to it.

Feasibility is judged on what your selections actually do when the project's own methods are
applied to them, and the declared columns are judged on whether they show the right rule was
applied. Both matter.

How the files are read: the schedule on E-621 is read from the sheet's text entities (TEXT or
MTEXT), not from its geometry. Workbook cells are read as stored values, so write numbers, not
formulas. Limits are judged with a small allowance for the rounding of the published cable
data: an ampacity may be taken as the vendor's tables print it or as their stated method computes
it, and a voltage-drop limit counts as met within 0.02 of a percentage point. In the ledger the
conductor line may be shown before or after any project-wide price adjustment.

You have no access to the verifier and no scoring oracle. Write a first complete version of all
five files early, then improve it.


## Verifier access (blind variant)

No verifier, oracle, or evaluation data of any kind is available in this workspace — the
only checks you can run are the ones you build yourself. Work from the brief and the
documents alone and submit your best final deliverable; it will be graded offline by the
frozen verifier on held-out instances.

1. Assignment
Sandhill Engineering Group requested a thermal resistivity investigation of the native soils
along the exterior duct-bank alignments of project P-4210 and of the
thermal backfill proposed for the encasement envelopes. Field work was performed 14-16 April
2026. Six thermal-needle probe locations were advanced along the DB-1 and DB-2 alignments to
a depth of 60 inches.
2. Results
2.1 Native soil
The native material along both alignments is a poorly graded sand with silt (SP-SM). Thermal
resistivity measured in place at natural moisture content ranged from 0.55 to 0.72 K.m/W. The
dryout curve determined on recompacted specimens is tabulated below. In accordance with the
practice of designing to the dry side of the dryout curve, the DESIGN thermal resistivity of
the NATIVE soil is 0.95 K.m/W.

2.2 Thermal backfill
The specified fluidised thermal backfill (sand-cement slurry, Section 31 23 23) was tested at
the supplier's mix design. Its thermal resistivity is stable with moisture content and is
0.60 K.m/W at and below 4 percent moisture. Both duct banks on this
project are ENCASED IN CONCRETE AND SURROUNDED BY THIS THERMAL BACKFILL for the full width of
the trench, so the material surrounding the encasement envelope, and the material whose
resistivity enters the earth-portion and mutual-heating terms of an ampacity calculation, is
the thermal backfill and not the native soil.
2.3 Concrete encasement
The red-dyed encasement concrete specified in Section 26 05 43 has a thermal resistivity of
0.55 K.m/W at the specified mix and cure.
2.4 Ground temperature
Ground temperatures were logged at 36 inches at two of the six probe locations between April
and June 2026 and ranged from 22.1 to 28.4 degrees C over that period, rising through the
record. The logging period does not span the summer maximum and these readings must not be
